meta.description: An unofficial, interactive viewer for AlphaGenome predictions: variant effects on genome regulation, with a SHAP waterfall, a tissue-by-assay heatmap, signal tracks, a splicing sashimi plot, contact maps and saturation mutagenesis. A static site that never calls the API.

home.title: What a variant does to the genome, predicted
home.lead: AlphaGenome is Google DeepMind's model that predicts how a variant changes the way DNA is read, and the Variant Atlas is its catalog of those predictions, precomputed. This independent, unofficial viewer reads them frozen in static files and never calls the API.
home.hero.note: The score places this variant among all variants in the genome. It is a prediction of regulatory effect, not a diagnosis.

about.title: About the data
about.how.title: How this was produced
about.how.p1: Predictions are queried locally with a personal key, frozen into versioned artifacts, and this page only reads those files. The AlphaGenome key is personal and non-transferable under its terms of use, so a public site cannot call the API live. The useful consequence is that the page loads instantly and spends no quota per visitor.
about.how.p2: AVI quantiles were recalibrated on 18 June 2026 and indel inference was corrected on 14 July 2026. Comparing artifacts from different releases is not valid, which is why each one carries its calibration epoch sealed in.
about.terms.title: Terms
about.terms.p1: Results derived from AlphaGenome are subject to the AlphaGenome Output Terms of Use. Non-commercial research use. Not a medical device, not medical advice, and not to be used for clinical decisions.
about.terms.p2: Everything shown here is a model prediction, not an experimental measurement.

card.panel.avi.subtitle: Variant position on the Atlas PHRED scale
card.panel.avi.hint: A PHRED of 20 places the variant in the top 1% of variants genome-wide. The scale is logarithmic.
card.panel.family.title: Contribution by family
card.panel.family.subtitle: Signed net and total magnitude of each feature group
card.panel.family.hint: The bar measures the group's total magnitude; the number on the right is the net contribution, which can be small if features cancel out.
card.panel.waterfall.title: SHAP attribution waterfall
card.panel.waterfall.subtitle: {n} features, grouped in four families
card.panel.waterfall.hint: Each bar runs from the cumulative score before the feature to the score after. Rightward raises the score, leftward lowers it. The vertical line is the base value the explanation starts from. Regulatory features are clickable: they lead to that track along the locus.
card.panel.tracks.title: Most affected tracks
card.panel.tracks.subtitle: Largest effect magnitude, up to {n} per modality
card.panel.tracks.hint: The small square on the left is the modality. The bar color is the direction of the effect: orange raises it, blue lowers it. The bar measures magnitude, not sign.

heatmap.panel.hint: Rows are grouped by organ system, not alphabetically: that way a continuous band of color means an effect specific to that system. Neutral gray is zero, not missing data. Every cell is clickable and leads to that track in the locus.

browser.panel.hint: The gray line is REF and the colored one is ALT. The shaded area between the two is the difference: orange where the variant raises the signal, blue where it lowers it. Scroll to zoom, drag to pan, press 0 to return to the full locus. Below an 8 kb window it switches to 1 bp resolution only.

saturation.panel.title: Saturation map
saturation.panel.subtitle: The AVI of the three alternative bases at every position
saturation.panel.hint: Each column is a position and each row an alternative base. The more a cell stands out from the background, the higher the AVI (in both themes). A column that stands out all the way through means changing that base matters, whichever change it is: that is how motifs show up. The scale is sequential rather than divergent because the AVI measures impact, not direction.
saturation.legend.title: AVI PHRED · impact
saturation.legend.ariaLabel: Sequential scale of AVI PHRED, from 0 to {max}.
saturation.readout.unknownVariant: AVI PHRED {phred} · {meaning}  ·  no frozen card: the pipeline freezes only a few variants per locus
splice.title: Splicing (sashimi)
splice.noData.title: No splice junctions in this window.
splice.noData.body: The SPLICE_JUNCTIONS scorer returned no observations for this biosample in this interval. A silent modality, not a failure: the same pattern as "no cataloged rsID".
splice.readout: {shown} of {total} junctions in this window, showing only those above {floor}
splice.hint.base: REF above the axis, ALT below: the difference in shape between the two halves is the signal. "Delta only" switches to a single row of signed arcs -red when ALT wins, blue when REF wins- for anyone who wants the exact magnitude instead of comparing two silhouettes.
splice.hint.touching: The {count} arcs that touch the variant position are shown at full intensity and the rest are dimmed; labels are assigned by |ALT - REF|, not by thickness, plus one on the largest arc as a scale reference.
splice.finding.title: The finding
splice.finding.method: The numbers come straight from the artifact: they are the {touchingCount} junctions whose ends fall within {footprint} bp of {coordinate}, among the {totalCount} that clear the {floor} floor in this window. They are also the top {touchingCount} when ranked by |ALT - REF|.
splice.legend.title: Thickness · magnitude (log)
splice.legend.ariaLabel: Thickness legend: logarithmic scale of junction magnitude.
contact.title: 3D contacts, REF vs ALT
contact.hint: Structure that is already there on top; what the variant does to it below. The outline marks the row and column of the variant's bin, exactly what the AVI contact map feature measures.
contact.legend.change.title: Change (ALT − REF)
contact.legend.structure.title: Structure (REF)
contact.legend.structure.note: its own scale: this is the existing relief, not a measure of effect
contact.verdict.invisible: Largest change in this window: {maxAbs}. Below the visible threshold ({threshold}): color cannot show it, and should not pretend it can.
contact.verdict.visible: Largest change in this window: {maxAbs}, over a fixed domain of ±{domain}.
contact.verdict.relief: The structure in this window spans {relief} and the largest change is {maxAbs}: {share} of the relief that was already there. The three-dimensional structure does not move.
contact.maxAbs.touching: That maximum does touch the variant's bin, {separation} away: {ref} → {alt}. It is the largest change in the whole megabase, and it is still this small.
contact.maxAbs.notTouching: That maximum does not even touch the variant's bin: it is {separation} from the diagonal, outside the row the AVI measures.
contact.maxAbs.outsideWindow: It falls outside the drawn crop (±{half}): it was measured over the whole megabase, not over what is drawn.
contact.bridge.title: Where the AVI number comes from
contact.bridge.text1: The AVI's contact map feature measures the mean of |ALT − REF| over all interactions of the bin containing the variant. It is the highlighted cross, extended to the whole megabase: {rowMean}. The cross draws the part of that row that falls in the crop, not the full row. And because the matrix is symmetric, its row and its column are the same set counted twice.
contact.bridge.text2: That number and this map are not the same quantity, and it is worth not confusing them: the AVI's is unsigned, a raw difference, and looks only at that cross. The map is signed and covers the whole window.
contact.biosample: Biosample: {name} ({curie}). The catalog's contact maps are 28, and all are 4D Nucleome cell lines: there is no primary tissue to choose from. A liver-derived line is the right biology for this variant, but it is still a cell line, not liver.
contact.magnify.noteOn: The domain is divided by {factor}. What is shown now is magnified, not what the comparable scale measures.
contact.magnify.noteOff: The default scale is the same across every locus: two variants are compared by looking at two maps.
contact.finding.title: The finding
contact.finding.method: It came from measuring, not from searching: the color domain is a pipeline constant (±{domain}) and was not fit to this data, so a flat map here means there is nothing to paint. The maximum was measured over the 1 Mb window given to the model, not over the drawn crop.

tour.step.0.title: AlphaGenome predictions, in the browser
tour.step.0.body: AlphaGenome predicts the effect of a genome variant across eleven molecular modalities. Its official library draws static images; this is an interactive viewer for those same results.
tour.step.1.title: Start from a locus
tour.step.1.body: Each locus is a one-million-base-pair window with its variants. Opening it shows the variant list with its AVI score.
tour.step.2.title: Where each number came from
tour.step.2.body: Every artifact carries a stamp of its origin, the client version, and its calibration epoch. If it says "synthetic data", it is development data, not real predictions: the banner always says so.
tour.step.3.title: The AVI score and its scale
tour.step.3.body: The AVI summarizes the expected impact on a PHRED scale. 10 means the top 10% of the genome, 20 the top 1%, and 30 the top 0.1%.
tour.step.4.title: What the score is made of
tour.step.4.body: The AVI is computed from 18 features. The waterfall shows how much each one contributes and in which direction, grouped into its four families.
tour.step.5.title: Browsing the locus
tour.step.5.body: The gray line is the reference signal and the colored one is the variant's. The shaded area between the two is the difference. Scroll to zoom, drag to pan, press 0 to return to the full locus.
tour.step.6.title: Ubiquitous or tissue-specific
tour.step.6.body: Rows are grouped by organ system. A continuous band of color means an effect concentrated in that system; color spread across the whole map means a ubiquitous effect.

data.note.chr11-116837649-T-G: Disrupts a TATA-like motif, heart (annotation from the Atlas capture).
data.note.chrX-101386224-T-C: Reduces SPI1 binding at the promoter (annotation from the Atlas capture).
data.note.chr1-109274968-G-T: Creates a CEBP motif, inverse effect (annotation from the Atlas capture). Checked against UCSC dbSnp155: rs12740374, the variant from Musunuru et al. 2010 that creates the C/EBP site at SORT1/CELSR2.
data.note.chr9-128226027-G-A: Splicing, glutamatergic neurons (annotation from the Atlas capture).
data.note.chr17-44001600-C-A: Disrupts an HNF1 motif (annotation from the Atlas capture).
data.note.chr12-54578515-C-T: The actual reference allele is C; the source documents gave T>C.
data.note.chr22-45969257-G-A: Disrupts a JUN/FOS motif (annotation from the Atlas capture).
data.finding.chr1-109274968-G-T: The three-dimensional structure of the locus does not move. The largest change anywhere in the window is a slight loss of one long-range contact that does start from the variant's own bin, but its size is a tiny fraction of the relief in the background map: the color barely leaves zero, and not because the scale was set generously, but because the domain is fixed and anchored to what it would take to reorganize a topologically associating domain. At this resolution a single base change rarely rearranges folding, and the model predicts that this one does not either. The published mechanism for this variant is transcription factor binding, not architecture, so a silent modality here is consistent rather than a failure. It is the same pattern the catalog already shows whenever a variant is asked about a modality that is not its own.
data.finding.chr9-128226027-G-A: Both upstream donors abandon the same acceptor site and move to the neighboring one, six bases upstream. The acceptor that carried almost all of the splicing in REF drops to practically zero in ALT, and its neighbor goes from residual to dominant. These are not two unrelated effects that happen to coincide: it is a reciprocal switch, and the four junctions involved are exactly the ones that touch the variant position. It came from ranking this artifact's junctions by |ALT - REF|, not from looking for a known case. Ranked by magnitude, these four did not show up at all: the thickest arcs in the window are constitutive and barely move between REF and ALT.
data.study.atlas-andino.label: AVI calibration and Indigenous American ancestry
data.study.atlas-andino.summary: Tests whether the same AVI PHRED buys the same strength of evidence for variants enriched in Indigenous American ancestry tracts as for matched European variants. The hypothesis is INFLATION, not underestimation: a variant that segregates on Indigenous haplotypes and is diluted within the aggregate AMR group receives a low FAF, and a low FAF is precisely the 'proxy impactful' label the AVI was trained on.
data.study.atlas-andino.power.note: Not measured. Gate G6 in document 03 decides whether there is power: if the extrapolated genome-wide count falls below ~2000 variants, the study is published stating that it fell short.
data.study.atlas-andino.limitations.0: PEL is inside the gnomAD v4 training callset: evaluating on PEL is evaluating on training data. It is reported as a separate arm.
data.study.atlas-andino.limitations.1: In a population that went through a bottleneck, variants travel on a few long haplotypes; treating them as independent is anticonservative. The effective number of haplotypes is reported.
data.study.atlas-andino.limitations.2: Radivojac et al. 2026 show a Simpson's reversal: comparing without conditioning on allele frequency makes almost everything significant. The analysis stratifies within FAF bins.
data.study.atlas-andino.limitations.3: Common Andean variants are enriched for adaptive function: if the AVI scores them high, it may be right. That is why the outcome is the calibration curve, not the mean.
data.study.atlas-andino.limitations.4: AVI quantiles were recalibrated on 2026-06-18 and indels on 2026-07-14. Only artifacts from the same release are compared.
data.study.atlas-andino.ethics: Only aggregate, open-consent data. No claims about individuals or about Quechua or Aymara communities, who did not consent to this framing. Follows the CARE Principles for Indigenous Data Governance.
data.study.atlas-andino.panel.estado.bod: The study has not been run yet. This page exists to show that the platform publishes a study without results without dressing it up as a result.

heatmap.search.empty: No biosample matches “{query}”. Tissues use their ontology name; organ systems their group name. Esc clears the search.
compare.title: Compare two variants
compare.lead: Two cards side by side, with the same measures. It only subtracts values each card already shows: no verdict and no similarity score.
compare.none: At least two variants with a card are needed to compare.
compare.invalid: One of the variants in the link does not exist.
compare.invalid.detail: Showing the default pair; pick another with the selectors.
compare.sides.title: AVI and cascade of each
compare.sides.hint: Both gauges share a scale and read the same way. The cascades do not: each starts from its own base value, which differs from card to card, so compare the order and sign of the bars, not their length from one to the other.
compare.family.title: Contribution by family
compare.family.hint: Sum of the SHAP contributions of each feature family. The last column is B − A: positive when the family pushes further up in B.
compare.feature.title: Features with the most weight
compare.feature.hint: The six features with the largest contribution in each variant, merged. A dash means that feature is not on that variant's card.
